stem:
Vivek asks whether a quadrilateral can have three interior angles of $90^\circ$ and a fourth interior angle that is not $90^\circ$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call the figure an "interior angle" only, without using the quadrilateral angle-sum.
Say that drawing four sides is what forces the angle sum to be $360^\circ$, instead of using the $360^\circ$ sum to constrain the fourth angle.
No: the four interior angles sum to $360^\circ$, so three right angles force the fourth to be $90^\circ$ as well.
Answer "yes" only because the stem prints the numeral $90$ three times.

teacher.key_rationale: Interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^\circ$, so three $90^\circ$ angles force a fourth $90^\circ$. Relabeling, reversing drawing and sum, or grabbing the printed $90$ all miss that hinge.
